result:
Review complete — written to `review.md`.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** (2 high-severity findings, 0 critical):

1. **`block-destructive-bash.sh`** — the new hidden-dir allowlist regex only excludes a curated list of sensitive dot-dirs (`.git`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.kube`, `.gnupg`, `.docker`, `.config`, `.claude`, `.env*`), but common credential files/dirs like `.netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.pgpass`, `.azure`, `.git-credentials`, `.cargo/credentials` aren't on that list — so `rm -rf ./.netrc` now silently passes where it was previously always blocked.
2. **`constructs-lib.sh`** — `find_local_source` dropped its slug-match validation and now returns the first directory in `search_paths` with any manifest, regardless of which construct it declares. This breaks silently whenever a user configures more than one entry under `constructs.local_source_paths` — every requested slug resolves to the same first-found directory.

One observation notes the `symlink-manifest.sh` traversal-check simplification is sound (no regression), plus a note that none of the three files gained test coverage for either behavior change.
